title: Definitions
body: User note:About this chapter: Codes, by their very nature, are technical documents. Every word, term and punctuation mark can add to or change the meaning of a technical requirement. It is necessary to maintain a consensus on the specific meaning of each term contained in the code. Chapter 2 performs this function by stating clearly what specific terms mean for the purposes of the code.

title: Scope
body: Unless otherwise expressly stated, the following words and terms shall, for the purposes of this code and standard, have the meanings indicated in this chapter.

title: Interchangeability
body: Words used in the present tense include the future; words in the masculine gender include the feminine and neuter; the singular number includes the plural and the plural, the singular.

title: Terms Defined in Other Codes
body: Where terms are not defined in this code and are defined in the International Building Code, International Fire Code, International Mechanical Code or International Plumbing Code, such terms shall have meanings ascribed to them as in those codes.

title: Terms Not Defined
body: Where terms are not defined through the methods authorized by this section, such terms shall have ordinarily accepted meanings such as the context implies.

title: Access (To)
body: That which enables a device, appliance or equipment to be reached by ready access or by a means that first requires the removal or movement of a panel, door or similar obstruction (see also "Ready access").

title: Air, Exhaust
body: Air being removed from any space or piece of equipment or appliance and conveyed directly to the atmosphere by means of openings or ducts.

title: Air, Makeup
body: Any combination of outdoor and transfer air intended to replace exhaust air and exfiltration.

title: Air Conditioner, Gas-Fired
body: A gas-burning, automatically operated appliance for supplying cooled air, dehumidified air, or both, or chilled liquid.

title: Air Conditioning
body: The treatment of air so as to control simultaneously the temperature, humidity, cleanness and distribution of the air to meet the requirements of a conditioned space.

title: Air-Handling Unit
body: A blower or fan used for the purpose of distributing supply air to a room, space or area.

title: Alteration
body: A change in a system that involves an extension, addition or change to the arrangement, type or purpose of the original installation.

title: Anodeless Riser
body: A transition assembly in which plastic piping is installed and terminated above ground outside of a building.

title: Appliance
body: Any apparatus or device that utilizes a fuel or a raw material as a fuel to produce light, heat, power, refrigeration or air conditioning. Also, an apparatus that compresses fuel gases.

title: Appliance, Automatically Controlled
body: Appliances equipped with an automatic burner ignition and safety shutoff device and other automatic devices that accomplish complete turn-on and shutoff of the gas to the main burner or burners, and graduate the gas supply to the burner or burners, but do not affect complete shutoff of the gas.

title: Appliance, Fan-Assisted Combustion
body: An appliance equipped with an integral mechanical means to either draw or force products of combustion through the combustion chamber or heat exchanger.

title: Appliance, Unvented
body: An appliance designed or installed in such a manner that the products of combustion are not conveyed by a vent or chimney directly to the outside atmosphere.

title: Appliance, Vented
body: An appliance designed and installed in such a manner that all of the products of combustion are conveyed directly from the appliance to the outdoor atmosphere through an approved chimney or vent system.

title: Low-Heat Appliance (Residential Appliance)
body: Any appliance in which the products of combustion at the point of entrance to the flue under normal operating conditions have a temperature of 1,000°F (538°C) or less.

title: Medium-Heat Appliance
body: Any appliance in which the products of combustion at the point of entrance to the flue under normal operating conditions have a temperature of more than 1,000°F (538°C), but not greater than 2,000°F (1093°C).

title: Approved
body: Acceptable to the code official.

title: Approved Agency
body: An established and recognized agency that is regularly engaged in conducting tests, furnishing inspection services or furnishing certification, where such agency has been approved by the code official.

title: Atmospheric Pressure
body: The pressure of the weight of air and water vapor on the surface of the earth, approximately 14.7 pounds per square inch (psi) (101 kPa absolute) at sea level.

title: Automatic Ignition
body: Ignition of gas at the burner(s) when the gas controlling device is turned on, including reignition if the flames on the burner(s) have been extinguished by means other than by the closing of the gas controlling device.

title: Baffle
body: An object placed in an appliance to change the direction of or retard the flow of air, air-gas mixtures or flue gases.

title: Barometric Draft Regulator
body: A balanced damper device attached to a chimney, vent connector, breeching or flue gas manifold to protect combustion appliances by controlling chimney draft. A double-acting barometric draft regulator is one whose balancing damper is free to move in either direction to protect combustion appliances from both excessive draft and backdraft.

title: Boiler, Low-Pressure
body: A self-contained appliance for supplying steam or hot water.

title: Hot Water Heating Boiler
body: A boiler in which no steam is generated, from which hot water is circulated for heating purposes and then returned to the boiler, and that operates at water pressures not exceeding 160 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) (1100 kPa gauge) and at water temperatures not exceeding 250°F (121°C) at or near the boiler outlet.

title: Hot Water Supply Boiler
body: A boiler, completely filled with water, which furnishes hot water to be used externally to itself, and that operates at water pressures not exceeding 160 psig (1100 kPa gauge) and at water temperatures not exceeding 250°F (121°C) at or near the boiler outlet.

title: Steam Heating Boiler
body: A boiler in which steam is generated and that operates at a steam pressure not exceeding 15 psig (100 kPa gauge).

title: Bonding Jumper
body: A conductor installed to electrically connect metallic gas piping to the grounding electrode system.

title: Brazing
body: A metal-joining process wherein coalescence is produced by the use of a nonferrous filler metal having a melting point above 1,000°F (538°C), but lower than that of the base metal being joined. The filler material is distributed between the closely fitted surfaces of the joint by capillary action.

title: Broiler
body: A general term including salamanders, barbecues and other appliances cooking primarily by radiated heat, excepting toasters.

title: BTU
body: Abbreviation for British thermal unit, which is the quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 pound (454 g) of water 1°F (0.56°C) (1 Btu = 1055 J).

title: Burner
body: A device for the final conveyance of the gas, or a mixture of gas and air, to the combustion zone.

title: Induced-Draft
body: A burner that depends on draft induced by a fan that is an integral part of the appliance and is located downstream from the burner.

title: Power
body: A burner in which gas, air or both are supplied at pressures exceeding, for gas, the line pressure, and for air, atmospheric pressure, with this added pressure being applied at the burner.

title: Chimney
body: A primarily vertical structure containing one or more flues, for the purpose of carrying gaseous products of combustion and air from an appliance to the outside atmosphere.

title: Factory-Built Chimney
body: A listed and labeled chimney composed of factory-made components, assembled in the field in accordance with manufacturer's instructions and the conditions of the listing.

title: Masonry Chimney
body: A field-constructed chimney composed of solid masonry units, bricks, stones or concrete.

title: Metal Chimney
body: A field-constructed chimney of metal.

title: Clearance
body: The minimum distance through air measured between the heat-producing surface of the mechanical appliance, device or equipment and the surface of the combustible material or assembly.

title: Clothes Dryer
body: An appliance used to dry wet laundry by means of heated air. Dryer classifications are as follows:

title: Type 1
body: Factory-built package, multiple production. Primarily used in family living environment. Usually the smallest unit physically and in function output.

title: Type 2
body: Factory-built package, multiple production. Used in business with direct intercourse of the function with the public. Not designed for use in individual family living environment.

title: Code
body: These regulations, subsequent amendments thereto or any emergency rule or regulation that the administrative authority having jurisdiction has lawfully adopted.

title: Code Official
body: The officer or other designated authority charged with the administration and enforcement of this code, or a duly authorized representative.

title: Combustible Assembly
body: Wall, floor, ceiling or other assembly constructed of one or more component materials that are not defined as noncombustible.

title: Combustible Material
body: Any material not defined as noncombustible.

title: Combustion
body: In the context of this code, refers to the rapid oxidation of fuel accompanied by the production of heat or heat and light.

title: Combustion Air
body: Air necessary for complete combustion of a fuel, including theoretical air and excess air.

title: Combustion Chamber
body: The portion of an appliance within which combustion occurs.

title: Combustion Products
body: Constituents resulting from the combustion of a fuel with the oxygen of the air, including inert gases, but excluding excess air.

title: Concealed Location
body: A location that cannot be accessed without damaging permanent parts of the building structure or finish surface. Spaces above, below or behind readily removable panels or doors shall not be considered as concealed.

title: Concealed Piping
body: Piping that is located in a concealed location (see "Concealed location").

title: Condensate
body: The liquid that condenses from a gas (including flue gas) caused by a reduction in temperature or increase in pressure.

title: Connector, Appliance (Fuel)
body: Rigid metallic pipe and fittings, semirigid metallic tubing and fittings or a listed and labeled device that connects an appliance to the gas piping system.

title: Connector, Chimney or Vent
body: The pipe that connects an appliance to a chimney or vent.

title: Construction Documents
body: All of the written, graphic and pictorial documents prepared or assembled for describing the design, location and physical characteristics of the elements of the project necessary for obtaining a mechanical permit.

title: Control
body: A manual or automatic device designed to regulate the gas, air, water or electrical supply to, or operation of, a mechanical system.

title: Conversion Burner
body: A unit consisting of a burner and its controls for installation in an appliance originally utilizing another fuel.

title: Counter Appliances
body: Appliances such as coffee brewers and coffee urns and any appurtenant water-heating appliance, food and dish warmers, hot plates, griddles, waffle bakers and other appliances designed for installation on or in a counter.

title: Cubic Foot
body: The amount of gas that occupies 1 cubic foot (0.02832 m3) when at a temperature of 60°F (16°C), saturated with water vapor and under a pressure equivalent to that of 30 inches of mercury (101 kPa).

title: Damper
body: A manually or automatically controlled device to regulate draft or the rate of flow of air or combustion gases.

title: Decorative Appliance, Vented
body: A vented appliance wherein the primary function lies in the aesthetic effect of the flames.

title: Decorative Appliances for Installation in Vented Fireplaces
body: A vented appliance designed for installation within the fire chamber of a vented fireplace, wherein the primary function lies in the aesthetic effect of the flames.

title: Demand
body: The maximum amount of gas input required per unit of time, usually expressed in cubic feet per hour, or Btu/h (1 Btu/h = 0.2931 W).

title: Design Flood Elevation
body: The elevation of the "design flood," including wave height, relative to the datum specified on the community's legally designated flood hazard map. In areas designated as Zone AO, the design flood elevation shall be the elevation of the highest existing grade of the building's perimeter plus the depth number (in feet) specified on the flood hazard map. In areas designated as Zone AO where a depth number is not specified on the map, the depth number shall be taken as being equal to 2 feet (610 mm).

title: Dilution Air
body: Air that is introduced into a draft hood and is mixed with the flue gases.

title: Direct-Vent Appliances
body: Appliances that are constructed and installed so that all air for combustion is derived directly from the outdoor atmosphere and all flue gases are discharged directly to the outdoor atmosphere.

title: Draft
body: The pressure difference existing between the appliance or any component part and the atmosphere, that causes a continuous flow of air and products of combustion through the gas passages of the appliance to the atmosphere.

title: Mechanical or Induced Draft
body: The pressure difference created by the action of a fan, blower or ejector that is located between the appliance and the chimney or vent termination.

title: Natural Draft
body: The pressure difference created by a vent or chimney because of its height, and the temperature difference between the flue gases and the atmosphere.

title: Draft Hood
body: A nonadjustable device built into an appliance, or made as part of the vent connector from an appliance, that is designed to: provide for ready escape of the flue gases from the appliance in the event of no draft, backdraft or stoppage beyond the draft hood; prevent a backdraft from entering the appliance; and neutralize the effect of stack action of the chimney or gas vent upon operation of the appliance.

title: Draft Regulator
body: A device that functions to maintain a desired draft in the appliance by automatically reducing the draft to the desired value.

title: Drip
body: The container placed at a low point in a system of piping to collect condensate and from which the condensate is removable.

title: Dry Gas
body: A gas having a moisture and hydrocarbon dew point below any normal temperature to which the gas piping is exposed.

title: Duct Furnace
body: A warm-air furnace normally installed in an air distribution duct to supply warm air for heating. This definition shall apply only to a warm-air heating appliance that depends for air circulation on a blower not furnished as part of the furnace.

title: Duct System
body: A continuous passageway for the transmission of air that, in addition to ducts, includes duct fittings, dampers, plenums, fans and accessory air-handling equipment.

title: Dwelling Unit
body: A single unit providing complete, independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking and sanitation.

title: Equipment
body: Apparatus and devices other than appliances.

title: Excess Flow Valve (EFV)
body: A valve designed to activate when the fuel gas passing through it exceeds a prescribed flow rate.

title: Exterior Masonry Chimneys
body: Masonry chimneys exposed to the outdoors on one or more sides below the roof line.

title: Fireplace
body: A fire chamber and hearth constructed of noncombustible material for use with solid fuels and provided with a chimney.

title: Factory-Built Fireplace
body: A fireplace composed of listed factory-built components assembled in accordance with the terms of listing to form the completed fireplace.

title: Masonry Fireplace
body: A hearth and fire chamber of solid masonry units such as bricks, stones, listed masonry units or reinforced concrete, provided with a suitable chimney.

title: Firing Valve
body: A valve of the plug and barrel type designed for use with gas, and equipped with a lever handle for manual operation and a dial to indicate the percentage of opening.

title: Flame Safeguard
body: A device that will automatically shut off the fuel supply to a main burner or group of burners when the means of ignition of such burners becomes inoperative, and when flame failure occurs on the burner or group of burners.

title: Flashback Arrestor Check Valve
body: A device that will prevent the backflow of one gas into the supply system of another gas and prevent the passage of flame into the gas supply system.

title: Flood Hazard Area
body: The greater of the following two areas:The area within a floodplain subject to a 1 percent or greater chance of flooding in any given year.This area designated as a flood hazard area on a community's flood hazard map, or otherwise legally designated.

title: Floor Furnace
body: A completely self-contained furnace suspended from the floor of the space being heated, taking air for combustion from outside such space and with means for observing flames and lighting the appliance from such space.

title: Fan Type
body: A floor furnace equipped with a fan that provides the primary means for circulating air.

title: Gravity Type
body: A floor furnace depending primarily on circulation of air by gravity. This classification shall also include floor furnaces equipped with booster-type fans that do not materially restrict free circulation of air by gravity flow when such fans are not in operation.

title: Flue, Appliance
body: The passage(s) within an appliance through which combustion products pass from the combustion chamber of the appliance to the draft hood inlet opening on an appliance equipped with a draft hood or to the outlet of the appliance on an appliance not equipped with a draft hood.

title: Flue Collar
body: That portion of an appliance designed for the attachment of a draft hood, vent connector or venting system.

title: Flue Gases
body: Products of combustion plus excess air in appliance flues or heat exchangers.

title: Flue Liner (Lining)
body: A system or material used to form the inside surface of a flue in a chimney or vent, for the purpose of protecting the surrounding structure from the effects of combustion products and for conveying combustion products without leakage to the atmosphere.

title: Fuel Gas
body: A natural gas, manufactured gas, liquefied petroleum gas or mixtures of these gases.

title: Furnace
body: A completely self-contained heating unit that is designed to supply heated air to spaces remote from or adjacent to the appliance location.

title: Furnace, Central
body: A self-contained appliance for heating air by transfer of heat of combustion through metal to the air, and designed to supply heated air through ducts to spaces remote from or adjacent to the appliance location.

title: Furnace, Enclosed
body: A specific heating, or heating and ventilating, furnace incorporating an integral total enclosure and using only outside air for combustion.

title: Furnace Plenum
body: An air compartment or chamber to which one or more ducts are connected and that forms part of an air distribution system.

title: Gas Convenience Outlet
body: A permanently mounted, manually operated device that provides the means for connecting an appliance to, and disconnecting an appliance from, the supply piping. The device includes an integral, manually operated valve with a nondisplaceable valve member and is designed so that disconnection of an appliance only occurs when the manually operated valve is in the closed position.

title: Gas Piping
body: An installation of pipe, valves or fittings installed on a premises or in a building and utilized to convey fuel gas.

title: Gaseous Hydrogen System
body: See Section 702.1.

title: Hazardous Location
body: Any location considered to be a fire hazard for flammable vapors, dust, combustible fibers or other highly combustible substances. The location is not necessarily categorized in the building code as a high-hazard group classification.

title: House Piping
body: See "Piping system."

title: Hydrogen Fuel-Gas Room
body: See Section 702.1.

title: Hydrogen-Generating Appliance
body: See Section 702.1.

title: Ignition Pilot
body: A pilot that operates during the lighting cycle and discontinues during main burner operation.

title: Ignition Source
body: A flame, spark or hot surface capable of igniting flammable vapors or fumes. Such sources include appliance burners, burner ignitors and electrical switching devices.

title: Incinerator
body: An appliance used to reduce combustible refuse material to ashes and that is manufactured, sold and installed as a complete unit.

title: Industrial Air Heaters, Direct-Fired Non-Recirculating
body: A heater in which all the products of combustion generated by the burners are released into the air stream being heated. The purpose of the heater is to offset building heat loss by heating only outdoor air.

title: Industrial Air Heaters, Direct-Fired Recirculating
body: A heater in which all the products of combustion generated by the burners are released into the air stream being heated. The purpose of the heater is to offset building heat loss by heating outdoor air, and, if applicable, indoor air.

title: Infrared Radiant Heater
body: A heater that directs a substantial amount of its energy output in the form of infrared radiant energy into the area to be heated. Such heaters are of either the vented or unvented type.

title: Joint, Flanged
body: A joint made by bolting together a pair of flanged ends.

title: Joint, Flared
body: A metal-to-metal compression joint in which a conical spread is made on the end of a tube that is compressed by a flare nut against a mating flare.

title: Joint, Mechanical
body: A general form of gas-tight joints obtained by the joining of metal parts through a positive-holding mechanical construction, such as a press-connect joint, flanged joint, threaded joint, flared joint or compression joint.

title: Joint, Plastic Adhesive
body: A joint made in thermoset plastic piping by the use of an adhesive substance that forms a continuous bond between the mating surfaces without dissolving either one of them.

title: Joint, Plastic Heat Fusion
body: A joint made in thermoplastic piping by heating the parts sufficiently to permit fusion of the materials when the parts are pressed together.

title: Joint, Welded
body: A gas-tight joint obtained by the joining of metal parts in molten state.

title: Labeled
body: Equipment, materials or products to which have been affixed a label, seal, symbol or other identifying mark of a nationally recognized testing laboratory, approved agency or other organization concerned with product evaluation that maintains periodic inspection of the production of the above-labeled items and whose labeling indicates either that the equipment, material or product meets identified standards or has been tested and found suitable for a specified purpose.

title: Leak Check
body: An operation performed on a gas piping system to verify that the system does not leak.

title: Limit Control
body: A device responsive to changes in pressure, temperature or level for turning on, shutting off or throttling the gas supply to an appliance.

title: Liquefied Petroleum Gas or LPG (LP-Gas)
body: Liquefied petroleum gas composed predominately of propane, propylene, butanes or butylenes, or mixtures thereof that is gaseous under normal atmospheric conditions, but is capable of being liquefied under moderate pressure at normal temperatures.

title: Listed
body: Equipment, materials, products or services included in a list published by an organization acceptable to the code official and concerned with evaluation of products or services that maintains periodic inspection of production of listed equipment or materials or periodic evaluation of services and whose listing states either that the equipment, material, product or service meets identified standards or has been tested and found suitable for a specified purpose.

title: Living Space
body: Space within a dwelling unit utilized for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, bathing, washing and sanitation purposes.

title: Log Lighter
body: A manually operated solid fuel ignition appliance for installation in a vented solid fuel-burning fireplace.

title: Lubricated Plug-Type Valve
body: A valve of the plug and barrel type provided with means for maintaining a lubricant between the bearing surfaces.

title: Main Burner
body: A device or group of devices essentially forming an integral unit for the final conveyance of gas or a mixture of gas and air to the combustion zone, and on which combustion takes place to accomplish the function for which the appliance is designed.

title: Meter
body: The instrument installed to measure the volume of gas delivered through it.

title: Modulating
body: Modulating or throttling is the action of a control from its maximum to minimum position in either predetermined steps or increments of movement as caused by its actuating medium.

title: Noncombustible Materials
body: Materials that, where tested in accordance with ASTM E136, have not fewer than three of four specimens tested meeting all of the following criteria:The recorded temperature of the surface and interior thermocouples shall not at any time during the test rise more than 54°F (30°C) above the furnace temperature at the beginning of the test.There shall not be flaming from the specimen after the first 30 seconds.If the weight loss of the specimen during testing exceeds 50 percent, the recorded temperature of the surface and interior thermocouples shall not at any time during the test rise above the furnace air temperature at the beginning of the test, and there shall not be flaming of the specimen.

title: Occupancy
body: The purpose for which a building, or portion thereof, is utilized or occupied.

title: Offset (Vent)
body: A combination of approved bends that makes two changes in direction bringing one section of the vent out of line but into a line parallel with the other section.

title: Orifice
body: The opening in a cap, spud or other device whereby the flow of gas is limited and through which the gas is discharged to the burner.

title: Outlet
body: The point at which a gas-fired appliance connects to the gas piping system.

title: Oxygen Depletion Safety Shutoff System (ODS)
body: A system designed to act to shut off the gas supply to the main and pilot burners if the oxygen in the surrounding atmosphere is reduced below a predetermined level.

title: Pilot
body: A small flame that is utilized to ignite the gas at the main burner or burners.

title: Piping
body: Where used in this code, "piping" refers to either pipe or tubing, or both.

title: Pipe
body: A rigid conduit of iron, steel, copper, copper-alloy or plastic.

title: Tubing
body: Semirigid conduit of copper, copper-alloy aluminum, plastic or steel.

title: Piping System
body: The fuel piping, valves and fittings from the outlet of the point of delivery to the outlets of the appliance shutoff valves.

title: Plastic, Thermoplastic
body: A plastic that is capable of being repeatedly softened by increase of temperature and hardened by decrease of temperature.

title: Point of Delivery
body: For natural gas systems, the point of delivery is the outlet of the service meter assembly or the outlet of the service regulator or service shutoff valve where a meter is not provided. Where a system shutoff valve is provided after the outlet of the service meter assembly, such valve shall be considered to be downstream of the point of delivery. For undiluted liquefied petroleum gas systems, the point of delivery shall be considered to be the outlet of the service pressure regulator, exclusive of line gas regulators, in the system.

title: Portable Fuel Cell Appliance
body: A fuel cell generator of electricity, which is not fixed in place. A portable fuel cell appliance utilizes a cord and plug connection to a grid-isolated load and has an integral fuel supply.

title: Press-Connect Joint
body: A permanent mechanical joint incorporating an elastomeric seal or an elastomeric seal and corrosion-resistant grip or bite ring. The joint is made with a pressing tool and jaw or ring approved by the fitting manufacturer.

title: Pressure Drop
body: The loss in pressure due to friction or obstruction in pipes, valves, fittings, regulators and burners.

title: Pressure Test
body: An operation performed to verify the gastight integrity of gas piping following its installation or modification.

title: Purge
body: To free a gas conduit of air or gas, or a mixture of gas and air.

title: Quick-Disconnect Device
body: A hand-operated device that provides a means for connecting and disconnecting an appliance or an appliance connector to a gas supply and that is equipped with an automatic means to shut off the gas supply when the device is disconnected.

title: Ready Access (To)
body: That which enables a device, appliance or equipment to be directly reached, without requiring the removal or movement of any panel, door or similar obstruction (see "Access").

title: Registered Design Professional
body: An individual who is registered or licensed to practice their respective design profession as defined by the statutory requirements of the professional registration laws of the state or jurisdiction in which the project is to be constructed.

title: Regulator
body: A device for controlling and maintaining a uniform supply pressure, either pounds-to-inches water column (MP regulator) or inches-to-inches water column (appliance regulator).

title: Regulator, Gas Appliance
body: A pressure regulator for controlling pressure to the manifold of the appliance.

title: Regulator, Line Gas Pressure
body: A device placed in a gas line between the service pressure regulator and the appliance for controlling, maintaining or reducing the pressure in that portion of the piping system downstream of the device.

title: Regulator, Medium-Pressure (MP Regulator)
body: A line pressure regulator that reduces gas pressure from the range of greater than 0.5 psig (3.4 kPa) and less than or equal to 5 psig (34.5 kPa) to a lower pressure.

title: Regulator, Monitoring
body: A pressure regulator set in series with another pressure regulator for the purpose of preventing an overpressure in the downstream piping system.

title: Regulator, Pressure
body: A device placed in a gas line for reducing, controlling and maintaining the pressure in that portion of the piping system downstream of the device.

title: Regulator, Series
body: A pressure regulator in series with one or more other pressure regulators.

title: Regulator, Service Pressure
body: For natural gas systems, a device installed by the serving gas supplier to reduce and limit the service line pressure to delivery pressure. For undiluted liquefied petroleum gas systems, the regulator located upstream from all line gas pressure regulators, where installed, and downstream from any first stage or a high pressure regulator in the system.

title: Relief Opening
body: The opening provided in a draft hood to permit the ready escape to the atmosphere of the flue products from the draft hood in the event of no draft, back draft or stoppage beyond the draft hood, and to permit air into the draft hood in the event of a strong chimney updraft.

title: Relief Valve (Device)
body: A safety valve designed to forestall the development of a dangerous condition by relieving either pressure, temperature or vacuum in the hot water supply system.

title: Relief Valve, Pressure
body: An automatic valve that opens and closes a relief vent, depending on whether the pressure is above or below a predetermined value.

title: Manual Reset Type
body: A valve that automatically opens a relief vent at a predetermined temperature and that must be manually returned to the closed position.

title: Reseating or Self-Closing Type
body: An automatic valve that opens and closes a relief vent, depending on whether the temperature is above or below a predetermined value.

title: Relief Valve, Vacuum
body: A valve that automatically opens and closes a vent for relieving a vacuum within the hot water supply system, depending on whether the vacuum is above or below a predetermined value.

title: Riser, Gas
body: A vertical pipe supplying fuel gas.

title: Room Heater, Unvented
body: See "Unvented room heater."

title: Room Heater, Vented
body: A free-standing heating unit used for direct heating of the space in and adjacent to that in which the unit is located (see "Vented room heater").

title: Safety Shutoff Device
body: See "Flame safeguard."

title: Service Meter Assembly
body: The meter, valve, regulator, piping, fittings and equipment installed by the service gas supplier before the point of delivery.

title: Shaft
body: An enclosed space extending through one or more stories of a building, connecting vertical openings in successive floors, or floors and the roof.

title: Sleeping Unit
body: A room or space in which people sleep, which can also include permanent provisions for living, eating and either sanitation or kitchen facilities, but not both. Such rooms and spaces that are also part of a dwelling unit are not sleeping units.

title: Specific Gravity
body: As applied to gas, specific gravity is the ratio of the weight of a given volume to that of the same volume of air, both measured under the same condition.

title: Stationary Fuel Cell Power Plant
body: A self-contained package or factory-matched packages that constitute an automatically operated assembly of integrated systems for generating electrical energy and recoverable thermal energy that is permanently connected and fixed in place.

title: System Shutoff
body: A valve installed after the point of delivery to shut off the entire piping system.

title: Electric Switch Type
body: A device that senses changes in temperature and controls electrically, by means of separate components, the flow of gas to the burner(s) to maintain selected temperatures.

title: Integral Gas Valve Type
body: An automatic device, actuated by temperature changes, designed to control the gas supply to the burner(s) in order to maintain temperatures between predetermined limits, and in which the thermal actuating element is an integral part of the device.Graduating thermostat. A thermostat in which the motion of the valve is approximately in direct proportion to the effective motion of the thermal element induced by the temperature change.Snap-acting thermostat. A thermostat in which the thermostatic valve travels instantly from the closed to the open position, and vice versa.

title: Third-Party Certification Agency
body: An approved agency operating a product or material certification system that incorporates initial product testing, assessment and surveillance of a manufacturer's quality control system.

title: Third-Party Certified
body: Certification obtained by the manufacturer indicating that the function and performance characteristics of a product or material have been determined by testing and ongoing surveillance by an approved third-party certification agency. Assertion of certification is in the form of identification in accordance with the requirements of the third-party certification agency.

title: Third-Party Tested
body: Procedure by which an approved testing laboratory provides documentation that a product, material or system conforms to specified requirements.

title: Toilet, Gas-Fired
body: A packaged and completely assembled appliance containing a toilet that incinerates refuse instead of flushing it away with water.

title: Transition Fittings, Plastic to Steel
body: An adapter for joining plastic pipe to steel pipe. The purpose of this fitting is to provide a permanent, pressure-tight connection between two materials that cannot be joined directly one to another.

title: Unit Heater
body: A self-contained, automatically controlled, vented, fuel-gas-burning, space-heating appliance, intended for installation in the space to be heated without the use of ducts, and having integral means for circulation of air.

title: Unlisted Boiler
body: A boiler not listed by a nationally recognized testing agency.

title: Unvented Room Heater
body: An unvented heating appliance designed for stationary installation and utilized to provide comfort heating. Such appliances provide radiant heat or convection heat by gravity or fan circulation directly from the heater and do not utilize ducts.

title: Valve
body: A device used in piping to control the gas supply to any section of a system of piping or to an appliance.

title: Appliance Shutoff
body: A valve located in the piping system, used to isolate individual appliances for purposes such as service or replacement.

title: Automatic
body: An automatic or semiautomatic device consisting essentially of a valve and operator that control the gas supply to the burner(s) during operation of an appliance. The operator shall be actuated by application of gas pressure on a flexible diaphragm, by electrical means, by mechanical means, or by other approved means.

title: Automatic Gas Shutoff
body: A valve used in conjunction with an automatic gas shutoff device to shut off the gas supply to a water-heating system. It shall be constructed integrally with the gas shutoff device or shall be a separate assembly.

title: Individual Main Burner
body: A valve that controls the gas supply to an individual main burner.

title: Main Burner Control
body: A valve that controls the gas supply to the main burner manifold.

title: Manual Main Gas-Control
body: A manually operated valve in the gas line for the purpose of completely turning on or shutting off the gas supply to the appliance, except to pilot or pilots that are provided with independent shutoff.

title: Manual Reset
body: An automatic shutoff valve installed in the gas supply piping and set to shut off when unsafe conditions occur. The device remains closed until manually reopened.

title: Service Shutoff
body: A valve, installed by the serving gas supplier between the source of supply and the point of delivery, to shut off the entire piping system.

title: Vent
body: A pipe or other conduit composed of factory-made components, containing a passageway for conveying combustion products and air to the atmosphere, listed and labeled for use with a specific type or class of appliance.

title: Special Gas Vent
body: A vent listed and labeled for use with listed Category II, III and IV appliances.

title: Type B Vent
body: A vent listed and labeled for use with appliances with draft hoods and other Category I appliances that are listed for use with Type B vents.

title: Type BW Vent
body: A vent listed and labeled for use with wall furnaces.

title: Type L Vent
body: A vent listed and labeled for use with appliances that are listed for use with Type L or Type B vents.

title: Vent Connector
body: See "Connector, Chimney or Vent."

title: Vent Gases
body: Products of combustion from appliances plus excess air plus dilution air in the vent connector, gas vent or chimney above the draft hood or draft regulator.

title: Breather
body: Piping run from a pressure-regulating device to the outdoors, designed to provide a reference to atmospheric pressure. If the device incorporates an integral pressure relief mechanism, a breather vent can also serve as a relief vent.

title: Relief
body: Piping run from a pressure-regulating or pressure-limiting device to the outdoors, designed to provide for the safe venting of gas in the event of excessive pressure in the gas piping system.

title: Vented Appliance Categories
body: Appliances that are categorized for the purpose of vent selection are classified into the following four categories:

title: Category I
body: An appliance that operates with a nonpositive vent static pressure and with a vent gas temperature that avoids excessive condensate production in the vent.

title: Category II
body: An appliance that operates with a nonpositive vent static pressure and with a vent gas temperature that is capable of causing excessive condensate production in the vent.

title: Category III
body: An appliance that operates with a positive vent static pressure and with a vent gas temperature that avoids excessive condensate production in the vent.

title: Category IV
body: An appliance that operates with a positive vent static pressure and with a vent gas temperature that is capable of causing excessive condensate production in the vent.

title: Vented Room Heater
body: A vented self-contained, free-standing, nonrecessed appliance for furnishing warm air to the space in which it is installed, directly from the heater without duct connections.

title: Vented Wall Furnace
body: A self-contained vented appliance complete with grilles or equivalent, designed for incorporation in or permanent attachment to the structure of a building, mobile home or travel trailer, and furnishing heated air circulated by gravity or by a fan directly into the space to be heated through openings in the casing. This definition shall exclude floor furnaces, unit heaters and central furnaces as herein defined.

title: Venting System
body: A continuous open passageway from the flue collar or draft hood of an appliance to the outdoor atmosphere for the purpose of removing flue or vent gases. A venting system is usually composed of a vent or a chimney and vent connector, if used, assembled to form the open passageway.

title: Forced-Draft Venting System
body: A portion of a venting system using a fan or other mechanical means to cause the removal of flue or vent gases under positive static vent pressure.

title: Induced Draft Venting System
body: A portion of a venting system using a fan or other mechanical means to cause the removal of flue or vent gases under nonpositive static vent pressure.

title: Mechanical Draft Venting System
body: A venting system designed to remove flue or vent gases by mechanical means, that consists of an induced draft portion under non-positive static pressure or a forced draft portion under positive static pressure.

title: Natural Draft Venting System
body: A venting system designed to remove flue or vent gases under nonpositive static vent pressure entirely by natural draft.

title: Wall Heater, Unvented-Type
body: A room heater of the type designed for insertion in or attachment to a wall or partition. Such heater does not incorporate concealed venting arrangements in its construction and discharges all products of combustion through the front into the room being heated.

title: Water Heater
body: Any heating appliance or equipment that heats potable water and supplies such water to the potable hot water distribution system.
